Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Church life

forgive verb

also pardon, forgive me

classical

Traupman 255, 311, 356
Cic. Att. 7.12.1: velim mihi ignōscās (Lewis & Short)

ignōscō, ignōscere, ignōvī, ignōtum

verb, third conjugation

forgive, pardon

With the dative of the person and the accusative of the thing: ignōsce mihi, forgive me (see excuse me).

Examples

  • sīc ignōvisse putātō mē tibi, sī cēnās hodiē mēcum

    consider yourself forgiven, if you dine with me todayHor. Ep. 1.7.69–70

  • Errāre hūmānum est, ignōscere dīvīnum.

    To err is human, to forgive divine.Traupman 255

  • Domine, quotiēs peccābit in mē frāter meus, et dīmittam eī? ūsque septiēs?

    Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? As many as seven times?Vulg. Mt. 18.21

  • Sī peccāverit in tē frāter tuus, increpā illum: et sī poenitentiam ēgerit, dīmitte illī.

    If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.Vulg. Lc. 17.3

Other words

  • dīmittō, dīmittere, dīmīsī, dīmissum — forgive (a debt, a sin)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mt. 6.12; Vulg. Mt. 18.21

    Classically to send away, let go; the Vulgate’s verb for forgiving debts and sins and the people who owe them (dīmitte nōbīs dēbita nostra, the Lord’s Prayer).

  • remittō, remittere, remīsī, remissum — forgive (sins)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Jo. 20.23; Vulg. 1 Jo. 1.9

    Of sins: quōrum remīseritis peccāta, remittuntur eīs (Jo. 20.23).

See also forgiveness, excuse me, I’m sorry, sin, repent.

SourcesLewis & Short: ignosco · Lewis & Short: dimitto · Lewis & Short: remitto
